content: Shift work sleep disorder is classified as a circadian rhythm sleep disorder. It primarily impacts individuals who frequently alter their work or sleep schedules or those who consistently work shifts outside of the traditional daytime hours. This repeated disruption of normal sleep patterns can lead to significant issues, including difficulty falling or staying asleep (insomnia) and excessive daytime sleepiness. Furthermore, a study conducted in 2007 by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) provided evidence suggesting that shift work may contribute to an increased risk of developing cancer.
